c.tagline: Ancient Song-dynasty capital of iron pagodas and night-market food.

taxi.fareNote: Metered from about ¥6-8; short hops across the compact old city are cheap. Pay by Alipay/WeChat or cash.

emergency.note: 110 reaches police, 120 an ambulance, and 119 the fire service; there is no single combined emergency number, and 112 works from mobiles to route you.

avoid.reason: Watch for pickpockets in the packed Gulou night market and use metered or app-hailed taxis rather than touts.

hood_desc: Kaifeng's downtown heart around the rebuilt Drum Tower and the Gulou Night Market, a maze of snack stalls, teahouses, and shops; the liveliest and most convenient base for first-timers who want the city's famous street food on their doorstep.

The historic northern district around Longting (Dragon Pavilion) Park, the thousand-year-old Iron Pagoda, and the Song Imperial Street, home to Kaifeng's grandest palaces-and-lakes scenery and its must-see Song-dynasty landmarks.

The old Hui Muslim quarter east of the center, wrapped around the Grand Xiangguo Monastery and the lanes that once held Kaifeng's historic Jewish community; a dense, atmospheric area of temples, mosques, and halal food.

Kaifeng's newer western district where the Millennium City Park (Qingming Riverside Landscape Garden) recreates a Song-era townscape; more modern hotels and quieter, greener surroundings a short ride from the old city.
A calm southern district named for King Yu's Terrace (Yuwangtai Park), an ancient earthen platform amid gardens; a quiet, local, budget-friendly area away from the tourist crush.
lodging: Manxin Hotel Kaifeng Drum Tower Square

water.note: Drink bottled or boiled water; tap water is not potable.

transit.hours: City buses and BRT lines run roughly 6:00 AM to 10:00 PM; there is no metro.
transit.note: Kaifeng has no metro; the compact old city is served by an extensive city bus network (including Bus Rapid Transit lines) plus taxis and DiDi, and most Song-era sights are within walking distance or a short ride apart.
transit.pay: Pay by scanning an Alipay or WeChat Pay QR code, tapping a rechargeable transit card, or cash (exact change, flat ¥1-2 fare) on board.

air: Zhengzhou Xinzheng International Airport (CGO) — nearest, about 80 km

car.idp: Not valid — China does not recognize the International Driving Permit; a temporary Chinese driving permit is required to drive.

train: Kaifeng North Railway Station (Zhengzhou–Xuzhou high-speed line, ~20 min to Zhengzhou)

airport.name: Zhengzhou Xinzheng International Airport (CGO) — nearest, ~80 km

transit.m: Airport shuttle bus / intercity rail to Kaifeng via Zhengzhou (~90 min)
Taxi or private car direct to Kaifeng (60-90 min)

tip.r: Tipping is not customary or expected in China; no service charge or gratuity is needed at restaurants, hotels, or taxis.
